title: Online collision geometry and paired head resolution pilot (not executed)
question: Can two controlled own streams distinguish current Android offline collision geometry and join-order resolution from plausible alternatives?
hypotheses: H0 geometry: physics::strikes uses head tip at r_head, forward probe r_body, strict 0.975*r_body anchor proximity and 3.666*(r_head+r_body) broad phase. It is client-derived, not an online fit.

H1 geometry: proximity multipliers 0.80, 1.00, 1.20 or combined-head/body-radius capsule contact predict distinct clearance bands. Score the full swept line/point candidates; 3.666 is a broad-phase gate, not a physical hitbox radius.

H0 order: after moving both snakes, oldest life is tested first and dies on mutual contact, with the fallen snake skipped for the newer life. H1: newest-first, both-die simultaneous resolution, or sequential move/test. Receipt order is not resolution order.
method: Exactly two 600 s invocations, sequential, at most two connecting/open/closing game sockets globally, with no other collectors running. At collection time retain the raw official list and decoder provenance privately; consider active listed endpoints in decoded order. Sequentially join one scouting identity on at most five candidates, record its first leaderboard population within 10 s, close and await close before the next; missing/dead probes rank last. Pick the smallest observed population, tie decoded order; require <=100. Scouting is a separately authorized, bounded preflight, not either pilot. Freeze a private endpoint-bound copy of this plan before either pilot; add only capture={server,scenario:paired-collision,seconds:600,bots:2}. Do not change scientific fields. Both pilots use that endpoint; stop if either client's first observed population is >100 or no leaderboard arrives before the hard 57 s pair budget. Save scouting rejects and failed pilots. Meet near the first client's spawn, not the world midpoint. Each 12-slot cycle runs ladder factors [1.3,1.1,0.9,0.7] times 0.975*r_body with probe0 then probe1 (the occupied side at staging is selected before contact, avoiding a forced body crossing), followed by four collinear head-on trials crossing probe role and first-join identity. Each trial starts fresh lives: await both socket closes, join first through own appearance, then join second. Stage tandem ladder with the probe behind the reference head and alongside its body at an initially safe lateral clearance; approach the requested parallel offset at <=0.12 rad, then hold within 0.6 units for 1500 ms. Reference cruises straight; the probe's nose passes along moving body anchors. This is a shallow tandem approach, not a perpendicular crossing through an infinite body line. Head-on staging uses a compact 1000-unit rail, opposing headings, and matched speed/size. Boost is permitted only before launch. Retain every slot, including abandoned staging and censored deadline slots; advance schedule after failure, never retry only favorable offsets.

sampling.unit: One paired encounter with both own-stream identities, source hashes, raw frame witnesses and achieved geometry; one invocation is a dependent acquisition cluster
sampling.selection: All preassigned 12-slot cycles until each 600 s deadline. Target >=2 qualified encounters per ladder factor per role (16 total) and >=2 per head-on role/join cell (8 total) over both pilots; these are feasibility targets, not power claims. No replacement invocations. Report attempted/launched/qualified/contact/survival/censored counts in every cell, including zero cells.
sampling.independence: Lives, samples and trials on one endpoint are dependent. Two invocations are insufficient to establish general online rules, server independence or confirmatory significance. Do not count 25 ms samples as independent trials.

exclusions: Qualification is prospective from launch through the event/hold: both own identities unchanged, body present in both streams, finite own and peer anchor ages in [0,350] ms, own versus peer predicted-head agreement <=25 units, each size 2..80 segments, size-radius ratio within 5%, speed ratio within 5%, positive speed, no held boost, unchanged segments and fam to 1e-6, heading within 0.16 rad of prescribed direction, and no control gap >100 ms. At least four live samples are required. Head-on launch additionally requires <=0.06 rad heading errors, <=2 units cross-track and >180 units longitudinal separation.

Abort and restage if either stream shows any unrelated snake head or body edge within 600 units of either controlled head. Test edges, not just anchors. Unknown hidden snakes remain a limitation. Abort within 900 units of the arena rim. Abort if staging exceeds 45 s, active run exceeds 12 s, size/heading/pose/boost changes, or tandem probe loses longitudinal overlap with reference body (lag >28 and <body extent minus 8).

No inference from cache disappearance alone. Require own game-over for contact. Keep 1000 ms post-event raw frames from both streams and preserve both observed death flags. Socket close, stale pose, unmatched speed/size, missing endpoint holds and capture deadlines are censored, never survivals. An absent peer may await a game-over for at most 100 ms after the last qualified sample; otherwise exclude.

Staging and boosting samples do not estimate geometry. Ladder contact during the approach gives an interval bound at the achieved offset, not a death at the requested final offset. Early unrelated death and any contamination are excluded even if consistent with H0.
validation: Before official collection, run node --test tools/fidelity/slither-paired-collision.test.mjs and the loopback host test, plus the deterministic Simulator API curve. Audit each acquisition with evidence.py. Reconstruct all incoming and outgoing bytes causally from both streams, preserve raw witnesses and hashes, and report achieved radii, speeds, offset ranges, headings, lag/body extent, control gaps and timing uncertainty. Compare frozen candidates on the same qualified encounters, with independent nuisance bounds of 2 world units position uncertainty plus speed*(anchor age + measured RTT)/1000 (speed in world units/s, ages and RTT in ms) and sensitivity at half/base/double bounds. Propagate timing along the observed velocity/heading paths, keeping perpendicular and along-track envelopes separate; also report the conservative isotropic envelope. Do not treat RTT as a measured one-way delay. Treat candidate predictions as unidentified whenever these bounds overlap alternative outcomes or no single body anchor/edge is isolated; never adjust time per encounter to favor a hypothesis. For order compare actual survivor identities against verified life join order in all four cells; require at least two qualified encounters per cell and candidate-discriminating mutual-contact predictions under all timing bounds before calling the pilot informative. Death receipt timestamps alone cannot establish simultaneity. Report all failures and counterexamples, candidate inconsistency counts and interval bounds; no p-values, fitted adoption or simulator change from these pilots. After pilot one stop for zero qualified ladder encounters or zero qualified head-on encounters, >50% third-party-aborted launched trials, any recorder/source/integrity fault, unexpected third socket, population >100 or repeated pair staging timeouts (three consecutive). Otherwise run pilot two; hard stop after 1200 s total pilot wall time. No threshold relaxation or extra captures. A route change requires v2 retaining these failures.
limitations: Not yet executed. Local synthetic outcomes validate tooling and the present simulator, not official server geometry or acquisition feasibility on a live server.

Protocol heads are extrapolations from anchor receipts, not simultaneous authoritative positions. Shared recorder time is not shared server time or one-way delay. Body contraction and packet batching are nuisance variables.

Tandem straight-body trials target the point-distance band. They generally cannot identify 3.666 broad-phase behavior or arbitrary swept intersections; head-on trials may not distinguish sequential phasing once uncertainty is included.

Population scouting, visibility, server load and repeated lives introduce selection/dependence. No unseen third party can be excluded by client-only streams. This task authorizes localhost tooling tests only; pilot and scouting execution are deferred to a separately authorized task.
